events.partner_name: Society of Women Engineers - San Diego
events.description:
SWE San Diego invites you to join us for a guided tour of the ASML San Diego Factory. ASML is one of the world’s leading manufacturers of chip-making equipment. The company manufactures complex lithography systems critical to the production of microchips that are used in many electronic devices including smartphones, laptops, and much more. The tour includes a short overview of ASML's history, products, and customers, an in-person tour of the EUV cleanroom, and a networking mixer with the option of visiting the ASML experience center.

• 5:30pm – Check-in to security & meet in SD6 Gathering Room
• 5:45pm – ASML Overview presentation
• 6:00pm – Walk to EUV cleanroom & gown-up

Space is limited to 20 SWE-SD members and the deadline to RSVP is Monday, November 14.

Information about the 2023 Southeast San Diego Science & Art Expo

Summary of event details:

What: Southeast San Diego Science & Art Expo

When: Saturday, August 12th - 10:00 am to 2:00 p.m.

Where: Valencia Park/Malcolm X Branch Library (5148 Market St, San Diego, CA 92114)


Upon Arrival: (MIrella or Dr. Nguyen will check in- PLease do not check in if you arrive ahead of us)

Please check-in at the CREATE booth upon arrival on the day of the event, so you can be provided your booth assignment and lunch vouchers/tickets. 


Booth details: We will have a 2 tables with electricity reserved.

SWE-SD will have a tablecloth for the SWE table.

Titanbot: please bring a table cloth for the robotics table; please bring extension and zip ties. bring extra pop up chairs if you want.

Each participant organization will be allotted 1 booth space (10 ft x10 ft space, unless special arrangements were previously made) to set up your experiments, demonstrations, and/or tech. Each booth will be provided the following:


  • one table + tablecloth 

  • Two chairs (additional chairs should be available) 

  • Canopy 



Although we will make our best effort to accommodate everyone’s requests for tables, we will be limited by supply and are encouraging groups requiring more than one table to please bring any additional tables they may require. Additionally, although most booths will be provided with canopies, we also encourage exhibitors to bring their own if they have one they would like to use. 


Power: (for those who indicated)

If electrical power has been requested, you will have access to electrical outlets at your allocated booth. However, please plan to bring (25-50ft) extension cords (and power strips) as some of the power boxes might be at a distance from your exact location (we will not have any to loan out). 


Lunch & Snacks:

All exhibitors will be provided with lunch, please let us know the number of people in your group when you check-in. There will also be a shaded area with water and snacks for exhibitors and volunteers. 



As a reminder…

Once again, due to supply limitations, please bring any additional tables (if needing more than one) you may need, your own canopies / tablecloths if you have branded ones that you prefer to use, and 25-50ft extension cords & power strips (if you requested power).


Parking

Free parking for exhibitors and guests will be available at the


Unloading & Loading 

There will be unloading areas at both sides of the event.


Load-in/Set Up:

7:00 am to 9:00 am

Note: There will be a lot of moving parts in the morning, including power, stage and venue set-up as well as buses/trailers pulling in on-site. Make sure to come with extra time to set up. Please be aware that opening remarks will be made promptly at 10:00 am. 


Take Down:

2:00 pm - 3:00 pm

Note: Booths can begin tearing down as early as participants deem appropriate. Keep in mind students and their families will be circulating consistently up until 2:00 pm.


Event Agenda:


Emcee: Roosevelt Williams III - Young, Black & in Business


Agenda for the day can be seen here



The 2023 Southeast San Diego Science & Art Expo will incorporate interactive science shows and demonstrations provided by UC San Diego, the Southeast San Diego STEM Ecosystem, and other local partners (hopefully you too!), as well as live musical performances, and art stations.

Some examples of demonstrations confirmed include exploration of engineering/physics behind low-riders and various exhibits that bring together science, art, and culture!

We invite you to get creative, come out, and help highlight the science behind some of the interactions we experience and see daily in our San Diego communities! Thank you for your interest in joining us and sharing some of your excitement, knowledge, and passion for science by hosting an interactive station or presenting a brief lesson explain landmarks or phenomena.

We welcome all activities that can be used to educate our community in any field of science, technology, engineering, math, and art.

This event is designed to inspire and engage the community in STEAM.  Activities and booths should be interactive and provide the opportunity for hands-on learning, ranging from pre-K to adults.

When: Saturday, August 12th, 2023, 10 am – 2 pm.

Where: Valencia Park/Malcolm X Branch Library (5148 Market St, San Diego, CA 92114, USA).

What: Southeast San Diego Science & Art Expo. A free, family-friendly science & art event for the general San Diego community.

Who: UC San Diego’s Center for Research on Educational Equity, Assessment & Teaching Excellence (CREATE), Malcolm X Library, SESD STEM Ecosystem, DoD STEM, Jacobs Center for Neighborhood Innovation, Elementary Institute of Science, and various (education, industry & business) community partners. events.partner_name: Society of Women Engineers - San Diego
events.description:
SWE-SD, FRC Titanbot/Eastlake SWENext, & FTC Roboctopi
FIRST Lego League Scrimmage
Pizza Lunch sponsored by SiSTEM
Meet-up with Engineers during lunch

Requesting Snack donations: email if you are interested in bringing some snacks.

Thank you Ms. Stacy Ganzer for spearheading this passion project!

Goal: To give Wilson Robotics members a chance to experience an unofficial QT since not all students will be selected to compete in the official FLL qualifying tournament.

Background: Wilson Middle School is a Title 1 school located in the low socioeconomic community of City Heights; the majority of students are on free/reduced lunch; families of refugees or immigrants. In 2018,  Madalyn Nguyen ( FIRST Dean's List Winner 2020) and Dr. Nguyen introduced FIRST Lego League to Wilson Middle School.  Since then, Wilson Robotics is thriving in its 6th year with their very dedicated STEM teacher and coach, Ms. Phet Pease. 

Due to limitations of coach and funding, Wilson Robotics teams are competing in the scrimmage to represent their school at the official competition.  Out of 50 Wilson members, only a limited # will compete in the official QT. Let's give these students an experience like an official QT!


Thank you FRC Titanbots for creating 9 trophies for the winning teams.

events.partner_name: Society of Women Engineers - San Diego
events.description:
For the past twelve years, Battle at the Border has served as Southern California's largest off-season FIRST Robotics competition, and has been co-run by Teams 1538, 2485, and 5025. Currently held annually on the campus of Cathedral Catholic High School, the competition is an opportunity for offseason fun and allows new team members to experience some of the thrill of an FRC competition. 

Battle at the Border is an off-season FIRST Robotics Competition hosted by Teams 1538 – The Holy Cows , 2485 – W.A.R. Lords and Pacific Steel 5025.

Off-season competitions are a great way for teams to get extra playing time with their robots as well as train new members. In addition, pre-rookie teams can use off-season competitions to see what FRC is all about.

Women have been responsible for some of the most significant advances in science, engineering, mathematics, and computing, and yet, only 28% of STEM professionals are women. Join us in discovering how to build a strong support network at your community college! We’re teaming up with two affiliates to host a session on the benefits and steps to kickstart a SWE (Society of Women Engineers) Affiliate at your college. Learn why creating this empowering community can enhance your college experience and career opportunities, and gain insights into how you can get started.

A SWE (Society of Women Engineers) Affiliate at your community college is a student-led organization focused on supporting and empowering women in engineering and related fields. It provides a network where students can connect, learn, and grow together through various activities such as workshops, networking events, mentorship programs, and community outreach initiatives. The SWE Affiliate aims to create a supportive environment for women pursuing careers in engineering, offering resources and opportunities to help them succeed academically and professionally.

Workshop Details:
📌 Location: Community Room, San Ysidro Library (4235 Beyer Blvd, San Ysidro, CA 92173)
🚀 Workshop Description:
In this workshop the students will design and build their very own paper rocket using simple materials like paper, tape, and straws. After they create the rocket, they will test it out to see how far and how high it can fly. We will experiment with different shapes and designs to discover what makes a rocket travel fast or high.
The big takeaway is that engineering is all about trying ideas, testing them, and improving them. That’s what real scientists and engineers do every day. By building paper rockets, they are learning how STEM helps solve problems, be creative, and understand how things move in our world.

This year, our SWENext Clubs and partner organizations will take the stage to share how they are STEMMing in their schools and communities. From robotics and coding to outreach, research, and advocacy, you will hear directly from students and leaders who are creating meaningful change.

✨ What to expect:
• Welcome remarks from SWE leadership
• Presentations from local SWENext Clubs and organizations
• Inspiring stories of innovation and impact
• Networking with students, professionals, and community partners

WiSTEM is more than an event. It is a space where we uplift young women and allies, strengthen mentorship, and build a STEM community where everyone belongs.

Come support our students. Come build connections. Come celebrate how we are STEMMing together.

We look forward to seeing you there 💜
